keyVerseText: These be the names of the mighty men whom David had: The Tachmonite that sat in the seat , chief among the captains; the same was Adino the Eznite: he lift up his spear against eight hundred, whom he slew at one time. The Tachmonite: or, Joshebbassebet the Tachmonite, head of the three. whom he: Heb. slain. he lift: See 1.Ch.11.11. whom he: Heb. slain
rootMeaning: The root of עֲדִינוֹ (ʻădîynôw) is עָדִין (ʻâdîyn), which conveys the idea of being slender or delicate, often associated with refinement or pleasure. This root originally denoted something slender, such as a spear, emphasizing elegance and precision rather than mere brute strength. The literal sense of 'his ornament' or 'his spear' suggests an object or attribute of distinction, highlighting both beauty and effectiveness.
usageInScripture: The word עֲדִינוֹ appears only once in Scripture, specifically in 2 Samuel 23:8, where it is used as a proper name, Adino, identifying one of David's mighty warriors. The translation consistently treats it as a personal name, reflecting a unique individual rather than a common noun. This singular occurrence underscores the word's specialized use, linking the name to a figure distinguished by notable valor and skill.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding עֲדִינוֹ as rooted in the concept of slenderness and ornamentation enriches our appreciation of God's provision of strength and distinction to His servants. The name connects the warrior's might with an element of refined grace, reminding believers that God equips His people not only with power but with purposeful elegance in their calling. This reflects the Christian truth that spiritual strength is complemented by the beauty of godly character, and that God's warriors serve with both courage and dignity under His sovereign hand.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Samuel 23:8, the phrase 'the same was Adino the Eznite: he lift up his spear against eight hundred, whom he slew at one time' highlights Adino's extraordinary valor and effectiveness in battle. The use of עֲדִינוֹ here personalizes the account, portraying him as a distinguished warrior whose skill with the spear—rooted in the word's meaning—symbolizes both his precision and strength. This enriches the narrative by showing how God’s mighty men were not only brave but also uniquely equipped for their tasks.
